decisions.reason: Operator training builds on the firm's established service offer, costs little to run, and supports machine sales, so it likely meets aspirations and gives no trigger for problemistic search.
The fourth rotary axis is a low-cost accessory that extends the firm's core machines and fits its modular engineering, so keeping it is the satisficing choice.

Hybrid additive post-processing is distant from the core and its results are uncertain, but industry growth and the firm's R&D slack let it carry this future-oriented product a while longer, though it is the most likely candidate for a drop.
The high-speed CNC milling line with several models sits at the firm's core competence and drives revenue, so it almost certainly stays.
The automatic tool change system complements the core milling machines and improves customer productivity, so there is no performance shortfall that would justify dropping it.
